name: Pituitary Hormone Deficiency Secondary to a Granulomatous Disease
aliases: Secondary Hypopituitarism due to Granulomatous Inflammation

criteria.description: Evidence of pituitary hormone deficiency confirmed by biochemical testing
MRI showing pituitary enlargement or stalk thickening consistent with granulomatous inflammation
Histological confirmation of granulomatous inflammation in pituitary tissue (if biopsy performed)
Exclusion of other causes of hypopituitarism such as neoplasms, infections, or autoimmune hypophysitis
Presence of systemic granulomatous disease (e.g., sarcoidosis, tuberculosis)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pituitary hormone deficiency with compatible MRI findings and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is definitive but not always feasible; diagnosis often based on clinical, imaging, and exclusion criteria.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to LH and FSH deficiency

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to pituitary hormone deficiencies
common.notes: Secondary to adrenal and thyroid hormone deficits
searchTerms: lack of energy from pituitary problems

common.symptomName: Headache due to pituitary mass effect
common.notes: Often from pituitary enlargement or stalk involvement
searchTerms: head pain due to brain mass effect
visual field cuts on both sides

common.symptomName: Polyuria and polydipsia from central diabetes insipidus
searchTerms: excessive urination and thirst from diabetes insipidus
polyuria and polydipsia due to pituitary disorder

common.symptomName: Weight loss due to hormonal insufficiency
common.notes: Secondary to adrenal and thyroid hormone deficits
searchTerms: unintentional weight loss from hormone deficiency
weight loss caused by endocrine problems
losing weight due to low hormone levels

occasional.notes: Related to adrenal insufficiency or mass effect

rare.notes: Due to adrenal insufficiency or SIADH

searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Meningismus or signs of meningeal irritation

laboratory: Low serum cortisol with low or inappropriately normal ACTH
Low free T4 with low or normal TSH
Low LH, FSH, and sex steroids
Hyponatremia due to adrenal insufficiency or SIADH
Water deprivation test consistent with central diabetes insipidus
imaging: MRI pituitary showing enlargement, stalk thickening, or mass lesion
Possible contrast enhancement of pituitary stalk
Absence of typical pituitary adenoma features
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; secondary to granulomatous disease
other: Histopathology showing non-caseating or caseating granulomas in pituitary tissue
Evidence of systemic granulomatous disease (e.g., sarcoidosis, tuberculosis) on biopsy or imaging

distinguishingFeatures: Autoimmune etiology without systemic granulomatous disease
Histology shows lymphocytic infiltration without granulomas
Presence of pituitary adenoma on imaging
Granulomas may be present but with infectious organisms

redFlags: Rapid onset of adrenal crisis symptoms
Visual field loss or sudden vision changes
